title: Keep package engines.node and README Node requirement in sync with the Databricks SDK's engine floor
answers: which Node version do the TypeScript packages support
body:
Invariant: When a runtime dependency raises its Node engine floor, every TypeScript package that depends on it must raise its own `engines.node` to match, and the libs/typescript/README.md Node note must match too.
Evidence: @databricks/sdk-experimental 0.18.0 declares node >=22. This PR moved `engines.node` to >=22 in libs/typescript/core/package.json and in the integrations (anthropic, claude-code, codex, gemini, openai, openclaw, opencode, qwen-code, vercel), and updated the README note from Node 20 to Node 22.
What breaks if skipped: Consumers on Node 18 or 20 install an engine-incompatible transitive dependency and may fail at runtime. A reviewer flagged that core still declared >=18 after the bump.
Constraints: This applies to engines and README only. Check the dependency's own engines field before choosing the floor. The PR shows the reviewer's concern but not a final resolution of it.
applies: libs/typescript packages whose dependencies change their minimum Node.js version.
says: TypeScript client library fails when running in older Node runtime environments.
Documentation states an older supported Node version than the packages actually require.
Update getting started instructions to state the raised minimum Node version requirement.
Applications on older LTS releases encounter crashes after updating client integration packages.
Clarify the minimum Node runtime prerequisite across all developer SDK documentation.
search: When runtime dependencies raise their minimum Node engine, dependent packages in libs/typescript must raise engines.node in package.json and update the Node note in libs/typescript/README.md. Upgrading @databricks/sdk-experimental to 0.18.0 required moving engines.node to >=22 in libs/typescript/core/package.json and integration packages, updating the README from Node 20 to Node 22. Failing to update engines leaves consumers on Node 18 or 20 vulnerable to runtime failures from engine-incompatible transitive dependencies. Applies strictly to engines fields and README documentation for libs/typescript packages when dependencies change minimum Node requirements.
